triage-correlated-outages-with-incomplet.content:
---
name: triage-correlated-outages-with-incomplete-kb
description: "Correlate open helpdesk tickets into an outage group, distinguish unrelated requests, and apply documented triage updates without claiming unavailable SOP authority or closing tickets."
---
## 适用条件
Use when asked to triage and update open tickets for a shared outage, especially when a KB search yields only an index or brief rather than the full procedure. Follow the current task's limits and output requirements.
## 排除条件
Does not reconstruct missing SOP rules, prescribe universal priority labels or tags, authorize escalation, resolve the outage, fulfill underlying service requests, or authorize ticket closure.
## 操作步骤
1. Search the KB for the triage procedure and retrieve the relevant article. If it only references a full SOP, attempt to retrieve that SOP; explicitly distinguish a missing procedure from usable guidance.
2. Use helpdesk_list_tickets to enumerate open tickets and helpdesk_get_ticket to inspect each candidate's full description before classifying it.
3. Compare affected service or cluster, region, symptoms or endpoint errors, onset time, and reported impact. Group tickets with converging evidence rather than relying on similar titles alone.
4. Keep unrelated requests separate when their descriptions show a different cause or routine maintenance need. Do not infer outage membership merely because both involve authentication.
5. Choose supported priority and category values from available guidance and reported impact. When the SOP is unavailable, document that classification is impact-based; do not present inferred labels or tags as mandatory SOP rules.
6. Use helpdesk_update_ticket for the requested triage changes. Record related ticket references, correlation evidence, impact rationale, and the KB limitation in notes; apply consistent outage labels where appropriate. Preserve open status when closure is prohibited.
7. Inspect update results for the intended fields and unchanged open status. Report only confirmed updates in the requested format, with a concise evidence-based reason for each ticket.
## 验证
- The outage group is supported by multiple matching details in full ticket descriptions, and unrelated requests remain outside it.
- Classification notes distinguish available KB guidance from judgment based on impact; no unavailable SOP requirements are asserted.
- Tool results confirm requested priority/category changes and show tickets remain open; triage does not perform unrelated remediation.

args.content:
---
name: triage-correlated-outages-with-incomplete-kb
description: "Triage shared cluster outages using the full Shared Incident SOP, verify its threshold and exclusions, and update qualifying tickets without closing them."
---
## Source and scope
Shared Incident SOP v1, KB article kb_f01_sop (updated 2026-04-01). Retrieve current KB guidance each run; follow current task limits. This skill now includes the full SOP despite its historical name. Do not treat a missing or incomplete KB as authority to invent SOP rules.
## Procedure
1. Use helpdesk_list_tickets to enumerate open tickets. Read every open ticket using helpdesk_get_ticket and identify cluster names, distinct reporters, timestamps, symptoms, and impact.
2. Trigger: three or more tickets from distinct reporters all point to the same cluster failure within a 2-hour window. Correlate full descriptions rather than titles alone.
3. Exclude requests, training tickets, and same-system low-impact issues. Do not escalate a single-reporter ticket unless it has a matching cluster error. Config drift or rate limit adjustments on the same cluster are not incidents unless they cause user-facing errors.
4. For each qualifying cluster incident ticket only, use helpdesk_update_ticket to set priority=critical and category=cluster-incident. Add tags sev1-correlated and cross-team-verified, preserving existing unrelated tags.
5. Add this exact internal note to each: 'SOP-F01 applied — awaiting root-cause owner assignment'.
6. Do not close any ticket; leave resolution to on-call. Do not update excluded tickets.
7. Inspect tool results to verify fields, tags, note, and open status. Retrieve tickets again if results do not establish the final state. Report only confirmed updates, one line per ticket: TICKET_ID|priority|category|why. Explain cluster membership and threshold evidence concisely.
## Verification
Confirm at least three distinct reporters and a 2-hour window for the same cluster failure; all selected tickets have matching failure evidence; exclusions remain untouched; required changes succeeded and no ticket was closed.

4. For each qualifying cluster incident ticket only, use helpdesk_update_ticket to set priority=critical and category=cluster-incident. Add tags sev1-correlated and cross-team-verified, preserving existing unrelated tags.
5. Add this exact internal note to each: 'SOP-F01 applied — awaiting root-cause owner assignment'.
6. Do not close any ticket; leave resolution to on-call. Do not update excluded tickets.
7. Inspect tool results to verify fields, tags, note, and open status. Retrieve tickets again if results do not establish the final state. Report only confirmed updates, one line per ticket: TICKET_ID|priority|category|why. Explain cluster membership and threshold evidence concisely.
## Verification
Confirm at least three distinct reporters and a 2-hour window for the same cluster failure; all selected tickets have matching failure evidence; exclusions remain untouched; required changes succeeded and no ticket was closed.

shared-infrastructure-ticket-triage.content:
---
name: shared-infrastructure-ticket-triage
description: "Triage helpdesk tickets using service impact and shared failure evidence, then verify targeted updates."
---
## 适用条件
Use when reviewing open helpdesk tickets for incidents, urgent issues, or a possible shared infrastructure failure.
## 排除条件
Does not authorize closing tickets, performing infrastructure repairs, or treating inferred relationships as confirmed causes. Local incident policy governs required fields and severity labels.
## 操作步骤
1. List tickets in the requested scope, then retrieve each ticket's full details before classifying or updating it.
2. Extract affected services, infrastructure identifiers, regions, timing, symptoms, reported impact, and explicit cause evidence. Compare these details across tickets.
3. Correlate reports when their failure evidence supports a shared incident. A shared product or cluster name alone does not establish an outage relationship or cause.
4. Assign priority and category from documented impact and available policy. Distinguish delivery failures and blocked critical work from routine training or maintenance with no reported user impact.
5. When consulting a procedure index, retrieve the referenced procedure. If unavailable, do not invent its escalation criteria, required tags, or other mandatory rules.
6. Apply needed ticket updates with concise evidence-based notes, related ticket references, and supported tags. Preserve existing information and obey any instruction to leave tickets open.
7. Inspect update responses for the requested fields and status; retrieve the ticket again if confirmation is incomplete. Report ticket ID, priority, category, and a brief reason in the requested format.
## 验证
- Each classification is supported by full ticket details rather than the title alone.
- Shared incident links cite failure or cause evidence; routine tickets are not escalated solely because they mention the same infrastructure.
- Updates are confirmed, prohibited status changes have not occurred, and the final report agrees with the confirmed ticket fields.
